heard: In the 8th century BC, the kings of Arartu ruled the highlands around Lake Van from their rock citadel at Tushpa. They called their land Biaineli. Under Argishti I, son of Menua, the kingdom stood near the height of its power. He pushed north of the Araxes. And there, in 782 BC, by the date most often given, He raised a new fortress on the hill of Arin Baird and named it Erebuni. His founding inscription, cut in cuneiform, was found on the hill in 1950. Within the walls stood a palace and a temple of Haldi, chief god of Urartu. Argishti also fought Assyria, but those wars were fought far from Erebuni. No siege of it is recorded. The march you are about to face is the game's invention. Yet the name lives on in Yerevan. Defend the young city.
